beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A photorealistic AI-generated hand reaching for a cup, which suddenly clips through the table.

beats.text: It’s like a magician who forgets to hide the strings; the model generates beautiful frames, but the objects drift, float, and vanish mid-motion.
beats.visual_focus: A wireframe skeleton of a hand showing the 'drift' where the object position deviates from the hand's grasp.

beats.text: Enter Ego2Act, a new benchmark that forces models to complete 110 multi-step tasks, while Ego2ActJudge acts as the automated, ruthless referee.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a model generation on the left and a 'Judge' score overlay on the right.

beats.text: The data is brutal: Humans hit 98% task completion, while the best SOTA models struggle to break 15%.
beats.visual_focus: A bar chart showing the massive gap between Human Consensus and current SOTA models.

beats.text: We are miles away from true world simulation. Follow The Model Verse to see who finally closes the gap.
beats.visual_focus: A final shot of a robot arm successfully grasping an object, rendered with perfect physics.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This actually slapped. You didn't waste my time with 'Today we are going to look at' and you didn't treat me like I'm five. The magician analogy in Beat 2 was solid—it perfectly describes that weird 'uncanny valley' physics glitch where objects just clip through each other. I liked that you gave me the hard stats in Beat 5; seeing that 98% vs 15% gap makes the problem feel real instead of just hype.
